Cautiously optimistic overall, but tempered by credit conditions. The FOMC emphasizes solid job gains, moderate growth, and inflation below 2%, with accommodative policy and a gradual, data-dependent path plus balance-sheet normalization. The July 2017 SLOOS points to softer credit demand and some tighter standards in key areas: banks reported weaker demand for CRE (including construction, land development, and multifamily) and for consumer loans (auto and credit cards), alongside tighter standards for consumer credit; demand for nonfarm nonresidential loans was largely unchanged. Residential real estate standards eased (jumbo/QM/GSE) and home-purchase/HELOC standards were mostly unchanged, offering a partial offset. Foreign banks reported tighter standards across C&I and CRE, even as they saw stronger CRE demand. This mixed-to-slightly-softer lending backdrop suggests some headwinds to spending and investment, reinforcing the Fed’s cautious, gradual approach and slightly reducing the positive tilt.
